title: Conditional central-context Q3 history composition
question: If every actual Q3 source difference has all four A^(a) D A^(-b) contexts at the one-step rate B, does the central insertion identity give a uniform B^n word bound and the corresponding factorial first-passage envelope?
method: Recompute the EXP-001045 onsite, edge and bond source polynomials in an independent primary and Fraction lane to obtain B=1382807/7168 from upstream inputs.
Declare the four common-core contexts M_(a,b)(D)=||A^a D A^(-b)|| for a,b in {0,3/4} as an explicit hypothesis rather than inheriting them from one-sided graph bounds.
Check A^a D_1...D_n A^(-b)=(A^a D_1 A^(-s))(A^s D_2 A^(-s))...(A^s D_n A^(-b)) on an exact diagonal finite fixture for all four contexts and word lengths one through four.
Insert the conditional B^n word bound into the separate two-orientation degree-six factorial first-passage EGF and compile Lean R230 for the group insertion and rational fixtures.
finding: Under the explicit four-context central hypothesis, the common-core insertion is exact and gives a B^n word bound; the recomputed EXP-001045 rate yields a conditional first-passage exponent eta=4148421/896000 for the declared fixture. The central-context hypothesis and the factorial Q3 recurrence are not proved.
decision_reason: This is a non-duplicative continuation after EXP-001047: it turns the repeated-factor boundary into an explicit sufficient central-context theorem for the actual Q3 source rate, while preserving the missing operator hypothesis as an open gate.
